entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 This appeal is filed by the claimant in O.P (MV) No.1215 of 2007 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Palakkad, claiming enhancement of compensation.
The respondents herein were the respondents before the tribunal.

2. According to the claimant, on 30.06.2007 at about 02.35 pm, while the claimant was riding his bike, a KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KL-15/4650 driven by the 2 nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit at the back of the claimant.
As a result of the accident, he had sustained serious injuries.

The claimant approached the tribunal claiming compensation of 40,00,000/-
3.
The first respondent/Managing director cum owner and the second respondent/driver of the offending vehicle entered appearance, but no written statement was filed before the tribunal.
Before the tribunal, PWs1 and 2 were examined, and Exts.A1 to A19 and Ext.X1 were marked.

The tribunal,
after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 12,63,550/- rounded to MACA NO. 1206 OF 2014 2026:KER:9476 12,63,600/- with interest at 7.5% per annum as compensation under various heads against the 1 st respondent/Managing director cum owner of KSRTC.
Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant has come up in appeal.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant and the learned standing counsel appearing for the respondent/KSRTC.
5.

The learned counsel for the appellant claims enhancement mainly under the following heads:-
Notional income:-

The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that though an amount of 5,000/- was claimed, the tribunal had taken only 2,000/- as the income of the injured , who was a milk distributor as well as a student.

It is further submitted that, going by the judgment in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the income of a Coolie, for an accident in 2007, is fixed as 6,000/- and sought for enhancement of income.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although the appellant had claimed only 5,000/-, to award just and reasonable compensation, following the judgment in Ramachandrappa (supra), MACA NO. 1206 OF 2014 2026:KER:9476 I find it appropriate to fix the income at 6,000/-.
Loss of earnings:-
On a perusal of the award, it is seen that the tribunal has awarded a consolidated amount of 15,000/- under the said head.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the appellant was only 20 years old and had suffered amputation of the left leg below the knee, as a result of which he could not continue with his avocation.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained as well as the age of the appellant, I find that a period of ten months can be taken for awarding compensation under the afore head.
Since the monthly income has been re-fixed as 6,000/-, the compensation payable for loss of earnings for a period of ten months is re-
calculated as 60,000/- (6,000x10).
The tribunal has awarded an amount of 15,000/- under the afore head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 45,000/- towards loss of earnings.

Mohammed Jaffar vs The Managing Dirctor on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18784773/
2 Loss of amenities:-

entities.text: Mohammed Jaffar vs The Managing Dirctor on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On a perusal of the award, it is seen that the tribunal has awarded only an amount of 25,000/- under the head loss of amenities.
Considering the age of the appellant as well as the loss of enjoyment in life, I find that a total amount of 75,000/- is to be granted towards loss of amenities.
Thus, there will be an MACA NO. 1206 OF 2014 2026:KER:9476 additional amount of 50,000/- under the afore head.
Pain and sufferings:-
On a perusal of the award, it is seen that the tribunal has awarded only an amount of 30,000/- under the head pain and sufferings.
Considering the age of the appellant as well as the nature of injuries, I find that a total amount of 75,000/- can be granted towards pain and suffering.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 45,000/- under the afore head.
Permanent disability/loss of earning power:-
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that as per Ext.X1 disability certificate, the medical board has assessed the disability of the appellant as 30%.
It is further submitted that, since there was amputation of the left leg below the knee, the functional disability could be fixed at a higher percentage.
On going through the Workmen's Compensation Act, the percentage of loss of earning capacity for amputation below the knee is fixed at 50%.
Accordingly, I find it appropriate to fix the disability at 50%.

Since the appellant is aged 20 years and the percentage of disability is fixed at 50%, following National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [2017(4) KLT 662(SC)], 40% future prospects is to be added to the income MACA NO. 1206 OF 2014 2026:KER:9476 now fixed by this Court, for calculating loss of permanent disability.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [2017(4) KLT 662(SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Following the judgments in Pranay Sethi (supra), and Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010(2) KLT 802(SC)], the compensation payable for permanent disability is recalculated as:
9,07,200/- (8,400x12x18x50/100) towards permanent disability.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010(2) KLT 802(SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The tribunal has awarded an amount of 1,29,600/- under the head permanent disability.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 7,77,600/- under the head permanent disability.

Future treatment :- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal has granted only an amount of 8,00,000/- under the head of future treatment,
without adequately taking into consideration the cost of purchase of a prosthesis as well.
The appellant has also produced documents to show that he has already incurred an amount of nearly 3,75,000/- towards the purchase, maintenance, and related expenses of the prosthesis so far.

Considering the age of the appellant, I find it appropriate to award an additional amount of 2,00,000/- towards future treatment,
which carry interest only from the date of judgment.
6. Though the appellant claimed enhancement of compensation MACA NO. 1206 OF 2014 2026:KER:9476 under the other heads, on a perusal of the records available, I am not inclined to interfere with the compensation awarded by the tribunal under other heads since it appears to be just and reasonable.

Since the appeal is of the year 2014, I find it appropriate to fix the interest @6%

3 per annum on the enhanced amount.
7.

Thus, the impugned award of the tribunal is modified as follows:-
Sl.
No Head of Claim Amount Amount Modified in Total claimed awarded by appeal compensation the tribunal 1 Loss of earnings - 15,000 45,000 60,000 2 Medical and 20,00,000 2,36,250 (not 2,36,250 miscellaneous modified) expenses 3

Future treatment 10,00,000 8,00,000 2,00,000 10,00,000 4 Bystander - 3,200 (not 3,200 expenses modified) 5 Transportation 20,000 20,000 (not 20,000 expenses modified) 6 Extra nourishment 10,000 4,000 (not 4,000 modified) modified) MACA NO. 1206 OF 2014 2026:KER:9476 8 Pain and sufferings 30,000 30,000 45,000 75,000 9 Loss of amenities 25,000 25,000 50,000 75,000 10 Permanent 10,00,000 1,29,600 7,77,600 9,07,200 disability TOTAL 40,00,000 12,63,550 11,17,600 23,81,150 rounded to 12,63,600

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part, and the appellant/claimant is awarded an additional amount of 11,17,600/- (Rupees Eleven Lakhs Seventeen thousand six hundred only) over and above the amount awarded by the tribunal.
The additional compensation awarded in appeal, except the amount of 2,00,000/- towards future treatment, will carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
The amount of 2,00,000/- awarded towards future treatment will carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of this judgement till realization and proportionate costs.
The first respondent/KSRTC shall deposit the said amount together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
The claimant shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, ADHAAR Card and bank details before the tribunal within a period of one month so as to enable the KSRTC to make the deposit as ordered above.
In case of failure to furnish details as above, it shall be open for the KSRTC to deposit the said amount before the tribunal.
Upon such deposit being made, the entire amount shall be disbursed to the appellant/claimant at the earliest in accordance with law.
However, it is made clear that the enhanced compensation will not carry interest for the period of delay of 102 days in filing the appeal.
